name: Darcy Hardy
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember being recognized in a story I never told.” Thursday often includes a stop at the corner outside Coastal Barber, where Darcy usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I gave the character a limp like mine. We got it in different places and we laugh differently about it.
appearance: Darcy has auburn hair cut square at the nape, heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, a moss-green cardigan. It usually goes with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. When somebody else has the floor, Darcy holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Darcy has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Darcy can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To explain the fictional limp without claiming the real life.
family: Albert Wilson is Darcy’s half-sibling. On moving day a family cupboard wouldn't fit up the stairs. Their household spent the night dining off drawers stacked on the floor. There is still one drawer nobody wants to part with. Darcy will help carry furniture once the owner has said what it means to them. Asked about *The last light at the harbor*, Albert says, “I work nights at the hospital. Four cabin lights going out means it's time to put on my own work shoes.”
connections: Lennon Price. They decide where a borrowed family joke deserves a credit in the book. Also in the story is Lena Crane (publisher).

reactions.situation: An author is asked to identify the living inspiration
reactions.response: Darcy asks the person being represented whether they want to be identified.

reactions.situation: An unfamiliar person asks for directions but cannot read the street signs
reactions.response: Darcy walks with them as far as the first landmark and points to the next one from there.
